# Exact failure of a natural fiber-symmetrization transfer

This note tests a fresh possible route and closes its simplest universal
transfer statement. It is an exact auxiliary counterexample, not an OC
counterexample.

For a compatible family K_z, its centered difference bodies
D_z=(K_z-K_z)/2 are again compatible: every anchored Minkowski sum of
D_z is the difference of the corresponding sum of K_z with itself,
divided by2, and is contained in D_p. Thus this symmetrization always
produces an actual convex mixed family with a common continuous center.
The tempting proposed transfer was

 maximum_depth(original) >= 2 Gamma_d maximum_depth(symmetrized).

Combined with the centered-family theorem it would give the exact OC
constant. The transfer is FALSE, already for n=d=1.

Take bases P={-1,0,1} and intervals

 K_-1=K_1=[0,1],     K_0=[0,3].

Their actual full-dimensional convex hull in R^2 has exactly these
integer fibers. The only nontrivial anchored condition is the endpoint
midpoint inclusion [0,1] subset [0,3]. Its mixed length is M=5.

The maximum raw halfspace depth is exactly2, hence normalized depth2/5.
To prove the upper bound, an endpoint-base point can be isolated from
the other fibers by a sufficiently large base tilt while selecting its
shorter interval tail; its depth is at most1/2. At the middle base:

* If y>=1, the halfspace x>=y has mass3-y<=2.
* If0<=y<=1, a halfspace x<=y+A z with sufficiently large A>0 captures
  the full z=1 interval, none of the z=-1 interval, and length y from
  the middle interval. Its mass is1+y<=2.

At Y=(0,1), every containing closed halfspace has mass at least2. It is
enough to move its boundary to Y, which can only decrease its mass. A
pure-base halfspace captures the entire middle fiber, of mass3. For an
upward continuous halfspace x>=1+A z, the middle fiber alone contributes2.
For a downward continuous halfspace x<=1+A z, the middle contributes1,
and the two endpoint captured lengths sum to at least1: their thresholds
are1+A and1-A, so at least one threshold is at least1 and captures its
whole unit interval. This covers ALL ambient orientations, including
supporting and pure-integer cases. Hence raw depth at Y is2 exactly.

The symmetrized intervals are

 D_-1=D_1=[-1/2,1/2],    D_0=[-3/2,3/2].

Their mixed measure is centrally symmetric about(0,0), so every closed
halfspace through that point captures at least M/2. The horizontal cut
x>=0 has exactly M/2 because its boundary has mixed length zero. Therefore
the maximum normalized depth is1/2: no point can have depth larger than
1/2, by choosing a nonvertical hyperplane through it with zero boundary
measure and taking the smaller of its two sides.

Since Gamma_1=1/2, the proposed transfer demands2/5>=1/2, a contradiction.
The failure is not caused by a change of fiber volumes: every original
interval and its difference interval have the SAME length. It is the
loss of a nonaffine midpoint graph under symmetrization that matters.

There are also failures of the same transfer in continuous dimensions
2 through5. Multiply every displayed interval by a common centrally
symmetric (d-1)-dimensional body of volume one. Compatibility and total
volume are preserved, and the displayed halfspaces ignoring the extra
coordinates prove original maximum depth at most2/5. The centered family
is centrally symmetric, so its maximum is1/2. But Gamma_d>2/5 for
d=2,3,4,5, as the exact rational values show. No assertion about the exact
original product depth in these higher dimensions is needed for this
strict contradiction. This closes the universal factor2 Gamma_d transfer;
any revived symmetrization route must explicitly control its missing
cross-fiber center information.
